fixes.explanation: Moses says, “…just as a man disciplines his son, so the LORD your God disciplines you.” (Deuteronomy 8:5) Notice who he picks: a father and his son. Not a boss and a worker. Proverbs says the LORD disciplines the one He loves, as a father disciplines the son in whom he delights. (Proverbs 3:12)

The Nile is a fair guess, friend. Water, Egypt, big river, I get it. But Moses is looking back at the wilderness, a thirsty and waterless land, and he says, “He brought you water from the rock of flint.” (Deuteronomy 8:15) That's a rock. Hard, dry flint. Nobody walks up to one of those expecting a drink, and that's the point.

Forty more years of wandering isn't what Moses says here, friend. Those forty years are behind them, and he's already told them what they were for (Deuteronomy 8:2). This warning looks at the road ahead. If they forget the LORD and go after other gods, Moses says, “…I testify against you today that you will surely perish.” (Deuteronomy 8:19)

problems.problem: It has 6 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.
It has 6 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.
It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
Saying discipline from a father comes with love makes a blanket claim neither passage gives. Proverbs 3:12 describes a father who delights in his son, not every instance of a father’s discipline.
The dead battery claiming it has charge has no clear connection to expecting water from a rock. The joke’s comparison does not share the action it is meant to illustrate.
